questions.question: How do you read and write files in Ruby?
questions.title: File I/O in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Ruby gives you several ways to read/write files. The block form auto-closes: File.open('path', 'w') { |f| f.write('hi') } (write) and File.open('path') { |f| f.read } (read). Shortcuts: File.read('path') reads the whole file into a string; File.write('path', 'hi') writes a string. Line by line: File.foreach('path') { |line| ... } (memory-friendly — reads one line at a time, doesn't load the whole file). Modes: 'r' (read, default), 'w' (write/truncate), 'a' (append), 'r+' (read+write). Always close files or use the block form (it closes for you). For binary, add 'b'. Encoding: File.read handles UTF-8 by default; pass encoding: 'utf-8' if needed.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know File.open with a block (auto-closes), File.read/File.write shortcuts, and File.foreach for line-by-line.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Opening a file without a block and forgetting to close (use the block form), or File.read on a huge file (loads it all — use foreach).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: File I/O: File.open(path){|f|...} (auto-closes); File.read/File.write (whole file); File.foreach (line by line, memory-friendly). Modes r/w/a. Always close (or use the block).

sections.title: Read and Write Safely
sections.content: Ruby gives you several ways to read and write files. The block form auto-closes: File dot open path w block f write hi (write) and File dot open path block f read (read). Shortcuts: File dot read path reads the whole file into a string; File dot write path hi writes a string. Line by line: File dot foreach path block line (memory-friendly — reads one line at a time, doesn't load the whole file). Modes: r (read, default), w (write/truncate), a (append), r+ (read+write). Always close files or use the block form (it closes for you). For binary, add b. Encoding: File dot read handles UTF-8 by default; pass encoding utf-8 if needed.

sections.title: File I/O
sections.content:
File.open(path){block} auto-closes; File.read/write whole file; File.foreach line-by-line.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  O[File.open path, mode] --> B[block: f.write/f.read; auto-close]
  R[File.read path] --> W[whole file -> String]
  F[File.foreach path] --> L[line by line: memory-friendly]
```

sections.title: File I/O
sections.content:
```ruby
# WRITE (block form auto-closes the file):
File.open('out.txt', 'w') do |f|
  f.write('hello\n')
  f.puts 'world'                # adds a newline
end   # file closed here automatically

# READ (block form):
content = File.open('out.txt') { |f| f.read }   # whole file as a string

# Shortcuts (whole file):
File.write('out.txt', 'hi')          # write a string; returns byte count
content = File.read('out.txt')       # whole file -> String

# LINE BY LINE (memory-friendly for big files):
File.foreach('big.log') do |line|
  puts line.chomp           # one line at a time (file NOT fully loaded)
end

# Modes:  'r' (read, default) | 'w' (write, truncate) | 'a' (append) | 'r+' (read+write)
# Binary: File.open('img.png', 'rb') { |f| f.read }
# Encoding (if needed):
File.read('utf8.txt', encoding: 'utf-8')

# WITHOUT a block you must close:
f = File.open('out.txt'); begin; f.read; ensure; f.close; end
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Opening without a block and forgetting to close (use the block form).
File.read on a huge file — loads it all (use File.foreach for line by line).
Forgetting 'w' truncates the file (use 'a' to append).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: File.open(path, mode) { |f| ... } opens and auto-closes the file.
File.read(path) reads the whole file; File.write(path, s) writes a string.
File.foreach(path) reads line by line — memory-friendly for big files.
Always close files — the block form does it for you; without a block, close in ensure.

Shortcuts: File dot read path reads the whole file into a string; File dot write path hi writes a string. Line by line: File dot foreach path block line (memory-friendly — reads one line at a time, doesn't load the whole file). Modes: r (read, default), w (write/truncate), a (append), r+ (read+write). Always close files or use the block form (it closes for you). For binary, add b. Encoding: File dot read handles UTF-8 by default; pass encoding utf-8 if needed. A common mistake is opening a file without a block and forgetting to close, when the block form closes for you, and File dot read on a huge file, which loads it all.
